newsitem.title: USA: CBOT CORN ENDS MIXED, MERRILL LYNCH SELLING NOTED.
newsitem.headline: CBOT CORN ENDS MIXED, MERRILL LYNCH SELLING NOTED.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed mixed with early gains pounded by aggressive selling, tied to profit taking by Merrill Lynch Futures, traders said.
Merrill sold at least 20 million bushels of December and six million bushels of March, traders said.

Hedge selling in early dealings began to topple an early rally with Cargill Inc a featured seller of four million bushels of December and also a seller of two million bushels each of September and March, traders said.
Bull spreading and profit taking pressured the deferred months to a lower close in thin dealings.
The lackluster close came after corn surged the 12-cent-per-bushel limit Tuesday on bullish input from USDA's August crop production report, traders said.

USDA Tuesday estimated 1997 U.S. corn production at 9.276 billion bushels, sharply below the July USDA World Board forecast for 9.7 billion and below an average of analysts' estimates for 9.554 billion bushels. The forecast was below the lowest analyst estimate at 9.375 billion.
Corn closed 1-1/4 cents per bushel higher to nine cents lower, with September up 1/2 at $2.62-1/4 a bushel. December closed 1-1/4 cent higher at $2.66-1/2.

Funds bought roughly 14.0 million bushels of corn with Griffin Trading purchasing eight million bushels of December, Smith Barney buying four million December and Prudential Securities buying eight million bushels of September, traders said.
In spread dealings, FIMAT Futures did three million bushels of December/September at three cents, premium December and ADM Investor Services spread one million December '97/December '98.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 80,000 contracts, above the 23,375 traded Tuesday.

In corn options, Cargill Investor Services bought 2,000 December $2.50 puts at five cents, Smith Barney bought 2,000 December $3.00 calls, sold 2,000 December $3.30 calls and sold 2,000 December $2.50 puts at 1/4 to 1/2 cent, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 30,000 contracts, below the 45,604 traded Tuesday.
